6.narrative: Willison's llm 0.32a3, by his account written almost entirely by the just-launched Claude Fable 5, keeps that model visible and proves real-world coding reach, but it speaks to authorship capability rather than intent-conditioned gating. No non-Anthropic lab published an intent-routed safety architecture today, so the subject of the prediction saw no movement.
6.remaining_gap: A rival frontier lab must ship and document its own intent-routed capability gating, not merely echo Fable 5's coding strength.

7.narrative: The rebound's two leaders were custom, non-merchant silicon stories: Alphabet tapping Intel to make roughly 3 million in-house chips and Nvidia evaluating Intel's 18A for future parts. The market rotated toward domestic foundry capacity and away from the GPU vendors, reinforcing the dual-track custom-silicon dynamic the prediction names, though no literal training-versus-inference SKU bifurcation was announced.
7.remaining_gap: An explicit training-versus-inference SKU split for custom silicon, not just generic in-house and foundry diversification, still has to surface.

8.narrative: DiffusionGemma is a 26B Gemma-4 open model running locally near 18GB VRAM quantized, over 700 tokens/sec on a consumer RTX 5090, with 256K context across 140-plus languages and native vLLM/Transformers/MLX/Unsloth support. That squarely fits the envelope of a Gemma-class model sized for a single high-end workstation GPU as a local-inference standard.
8.remaining_gap: It is Mixture-of-Experts rather than dense, ships 256K not 1M context, and its GGUF/llama.cpp edge path is still only listed as coming.
